faq_title: Questions we get asked about Bekamak manual band saws

faq.q: What does “gravity feed” mean on a band saw?
faq.a: The saw bow descends under its own weight; a hydraulic cylinder with an adjustable valve controls how fast it drops, so the operator sets the cutting pressure for the material. After the cut the operator lifts the bow back up by hand.

faq.q: Can a manual band saw cut miters?
faq.a: Yes. The BMS 230DG and 270DG heads swivel to both sides — +60° to the right and −45° to the left — with an angle scale and fast stops at 30°, 45° and 60°, so one setup covers most structural miters.

faq.q: When should I move up to a semi-automatic saw?
faq.a: When you cut more than a few dozen pieces a day, or when the operator is tied up holding the bow. A semi-automatic saw clamps hydraulically, cuts at a preset feed and lifts the bow by itself, so the operator only loads material. See the Bekamak semi-automatic band saws page.

faq.q: What voltage do these saws run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V with a CSA-approved electrical panel; 208 V, 240 V or 480 V 3-phase are available on request.
